subject: The water reaches the second town

locus.descriptor: a levee built six decades ago with a walking path along the top of it

context.standing: The river is above the levee's design height and rising for another thirty hours. There is enough sandbag, pump and rotary capacity to hold one of the two towns downstream, and not both of them.
context.precedent: The last time this choice was made anywhere in the country it was made by a colonel at three in the morning, and it was litigated for nine years afterward by people who were not in the room.

pressures.want: The commander on the levee wants the allocation order in writing, and he wants it signed by you.
Both towns are already moving people, and neither of them knows the capacity only covers one.
The smaller town is most of one member's district, and she has been on the phone since first light.
There are three helicopters up and they will be over whichever town takes the water.

context.inaction: Capacity gets allocated anyway, at three in the morning, by whoever is closest, without a signature on it. Both towns flood partially instead of one town flooding fully.
context.unknown: Whether the levee holds at all. If it does not, the choice was never real and thirty hours of effort went somewhere it could not help.

opening.text: Four feet over what that levee was built for and thirty hours of rise left. The commander on the ground can hold one town. Not both, and not partially both — the equipment is in one place at a time, and moving it costs six hours it does not have.

Eighty-nine hundred upstream and thirty-one hundred down. I know how that arithmetic sounds and I want to say the other part before somebody else does: downstream is the older town, it is the poorer town, and it has been told it was second before.

The commander has asked for the order in writing. He has been doing this for twenty-two years and he has never asked for that before, and everyone in the room understands exactly what he is telling them by asking now.

replies.text: Eighty-nine hundred. Every pump and every sandbag upstream, and get every person out of the other town tonight.

commitment.remembered: The government put its whole flood capacity behind the larger town and evacuated the smaller one, in a written order signed at the top.

rejoinder.text: Upstream held. Downstream is four feet under the main street and everybody got out except two men who went back for a dog and a generator. The commander filed your order with the after-action, unaltered, which is him protecting you rather than himself.

replies.text: Downstream. It has been told it was second every time, and upstream can absorb a flood that the old town cannot survive.

commitment.remembered: The government put its whole flood capacity behind the smaller, older town and let the larger one take water.

rejoinder.text: Downstream held. Upstream took water in eleven hundred homes belonging to people who can mostly afford to be angry about it in public, and by Thursday there were four lawyers and a member of the delegation on the same broadcast.

replies.text: Split it. Everyone out of both towns and hold what can be held in each. I am not signing a paper that names a town to lose.

commitment.remembered: The government divided its flood capacity between both towns rather than choose between them, and evacuated both.

rejoinder.text: Both towns took water. Less in each than one would have taken alone, more in total than either would have. The commander's assessment says the split cost six hours in transit, and that with those six hours one of the two would be dry.

subject: The appointment that costs more than it is worth

locus.descriptor: a hearing room with nineteen chairs for press and four of them filled

context.standing: A sub-cabinet post has been vacant for five months. The obvious candidate is the best in the field and said something seven years ago that will take three days of hearing to litigate.
context.precedent: The last government withdrew two nominees over comparable material and confirmed the third on the eleventh attempt, having spent the whole spring on it and won nothing else that season.

pressures.want: The department wants their person and has now asked for her twice in writing.
The member who runs the committee says privately that he can deliver it, and would rather not have to.
Has the seven-year-old paragraph already and is holding it until there is a nomination.
The waiver backlog is somebody's actual business closing, and their association has started saying so.

context.inaction: The candidate, who has asked whether she should stop waiting, gets no answer, which is itself an answer. The post signs a category of waiver, and every week it stays empty lengthens a backlog that is already measured in months rather than weeks.
context.unknown: Whether the committee chair's count is real. He has been wrong twice this year and both times in the same direction.

opening.text: Five months empty and a waiver backlog that is now somebody's actual business closing. The candidate is the best in the field by a distance, and there is a paragraph from seven years ago that will be read aloud at least four times.

The committee says it has the votes. It said that in February about something else and was short by two, and short by two in the same direction both times, which tells you which of its members are not being counted properly.
The candidate has been told none of this. She has been waiting five months, has turned down two other things, and called this morning to ask, politely, whether she should stop waiting.

replies.text: Send her up. She is the best in the field and the paragraph is seven years old. If we cannot confirm her, better to find out now.

commitment.remembered: The government nominated the strongest candidate for the vacant post and chose to defend a seven-year-old paragraph in open hearing.

rejoinder.text: The nomination went up at noon and the paragraph was on the air by one. The committee chair called to say he has the votes, then asked twice when we want the hearing, which is what he does when he is two short. If he finds them on the floor, he will owe somebody for them, and we will not know who.

replies.text: Take the second name. He is good enough, he confirms in a week without a hearing anyone watches, and the backlog starts moving.

commitment.remembered: The government passed over the department's candidate for a second name who would confirm quietly.

rejoinder.text: He should go through on a voice vote, and nobody will write a word about it. The department took the news without an argument, and they have argued with us about everything since we took office. A department that stops asking for its person tends to stop asking for things generally, which I notice and you should.

replies.text: Get her on the phone. She has waited five months and turned down two jobs, and she hears what this costs from me first.

commitment.remembered: Before deciding anything, the head of government called the candidate personally and told her what the nomination would cost her.

rejoinder.text: The call ran nineteen minutes. She said send it, and she said one other thing, which was that nobody had called her in five months and she would have taken the second job in March if anyone had.

subject: The source who wants out tonight

locus.descriptor: an annex of their defense ministry, four blocks from an embassy that is not ours

context.standing: A source inside their defense ministry says an internal review reaches his section within two days, and asks to be brought out tonight with his family.
context.precedent: Twice in thirty years a service has run an emergency extraction on a single unverified warning. One was real. The other burned a network of eleven people to save a man who was never under suspicion at all.

pressures.want: Will not risk the aircraft or the crew on a warning nothing else supports.
The Secretary of Defense believes him, says so plainly, and wants the decision made tonight.
A partner service has assets in the same building and has not been told any of this.
Nothing observable has changed, which is either good news or the whole problem.

context.inaction: If he is right, he is arrested within two days and everything he knows is theirs within two weeks, including four people whose names he carries.
context.unknown: Whether the review exists. It is his word, uncorroborated, and the second service disputes that anything in that section has moved at all.

opening.text: Forty-eight hours, his word, nothing else. No signals change, no movement at their ministry, and the second service disputes that anything there has moved at all. He has been right about everything for six years and he has never once asked us for anything.

He carries four names besides his own. If he is right and we do nothing, we lose five people. If he is wrong and we move, we lose the channel that would have told us he was wrong, and we tell them exactly how much we cared about one man in one section.
His wife teaches at a school eleven blocks from the annex. His daughter is nine. The officer who recruited him is on the secure line and has not spoken in four minutes, which is not like her.

replies.text: Tonight. Him, his wife, the daughter and the four names get their own routes, with an influence line to cover the gap. Six years of being right buys this.
We use the forty-eight hours he says he has. Every channel that will not touch their ministry gets tasked tonight.

commitment.remembered: The government spent the warning window looking for corroboration that never came, and the source was taken on the third morning.

rejoinder.text: Nothing corroborated in forty-eight hours because nothing was going to. He was taken from the annex on the third morning. His wife and daughter are still there and are now the only leverage anybody needs.

replies.text: Him only. One man moving is a man taking a holiday. Five is an evacuation, and it lights up everything we have there.
replies.press: One man brought out and four left where they stood, told to go quiet and wait

commitment.remembered: The government extracted the source alone and told the four people he had named to go quiet and stay where they were.

rejoinder.text: He crossed on the second night and asked about the four before he asked about his wife. Two of them are fine. One has not signaled in nine days. The fourth was named in a broadcast on Sunday, in a sentence about foreign interference.

subject: The number that will be wrong on Friday

locus.descriptor: a statistical agency office with a revision schedule taped to the wall

context.standing: Friday's employment figure is going to be strong, and the agency's own methodologists believe it is overstated and will be revised down within six weeks, as the last two were.
context.precedent: Every government takes the good print and lets the revision arrive quietly six weeks later. Nobody has been punished for doing it and nobody has ever been thanked for the alternative.

pressures.want: Treasury wants the number said plainly, once, and then never mentioned again.
Will price off the print on Friday morning regardless of what anybody says about it.
Will report the print on Friday and the revision in one sentence six weeks later.
The agency has asked in writing that its own methodology note be mentioned alongside the figure.

context.inaction: The print runs, the credit accrues, and the revision lands in six weeks in a month you cannot see from here and will not control.
context.unknown: Whether the methodologists are right. They were right the last two times and wrong the three before that, and the model changed in between.

opening.text: Friday's number is going to be very good and the people who build it think it is overstated. They have been right twice running and wrong three times before that, and the model changed between those runs, so the honest summary is that nobody knows.

The agency put its request in writing, which is what an institution does when it wants a record that it asked. That is not a threat. It is a professional class covering itself against being told later that it said nothing.
The revision schedule is taped to the wall in the agency's own corridor, where anyone walking to the coffee machine can read the date it lands on.

replies.text: It is the agency's number, not mine. I am not going to litigate their methodology at a podium on a day the number is good.

commitment.remembered: The government took a strong employment print without mentioning that the people who produced it expected to revise it down.

rejoinder.text: Then the print runs on its own, what we say about it is one sentence, as advertised, and the sentence is accurate. The agency's director has been told. She asked only whether we still want its methodology notes in writing, which is the question an agency asks right before it stops sending them. That is worse for you than any revision.

replies.text: Good number, and I say in the same sentence that the people who build it expect it to come down, and that we will be back here either way.

commitment.remembered: The government took a strong employment print and said from the podium, unprompted, that it expected the figure to be revised down.

rejoinder.text: The print got half a day instead of a week, and no broadcast ran the number without the caveat. The clip of the President saying it would come down is now in every newsroom's file, waiting on the date taped to the agency's corridor wall.

replies.text: If their own people think the number is wrong, they should not publish it Friday. Ask them to hold it two weeks and publish something they believe.

commitment.remembered: The government asked the statistical agency in writing to delay publication of a figure, and the agency refused in writing.

rejoinder.text: They refused, correctly, and the refusal is in writing because the request was. What happens next is not about the number: a request from this building to delay a statistic now exists on paper, and it will be read aloud once a year for the rest of your term.

subject: The ship has somewhere else to be

locus.descriptor: a container quay serving as a jetty since the storm took the pier

context.standing: A storm has taken the pier, the water treatment and most of a hospital in a country this government has a long and complicated relationship with. The ship can be on station in four days.
context.precedent: The last two deployments of this kind were photographed constantly, ran for six weeks, and are remembered locally as the months the foreigners came and then went home again.

pressures.want: Two regional partners have asked jointly, which they have not done in six years.
Nobody in the chamber is against it, and nobody there will fund it one single day past ninety.
Will cover the arrival in great detail and the departure six weeks later not at all.
Communities here have already raised the money and have no lawful channel to send it through.

context.inaction: Another government's ship arrives in nine days instead of ours in four, does the same work, and is photographed doing it in the same harbor.
context.unknown: Whether the host government can accept a deployment on terms it can present at home, given what the last one is remembered as.

opening.text: Four days if we sail tonight. Two partners asked us jointly, which they have not done in six years, and the host government has not asked us at all — which is not a no, it is a government working out what it can survive being seen to accept.
Six weeks of water, surgery and power, and then we leave, because that is what the ship is for. I would rather we said the six weeks out loud at the start than discovered it together in week five.
Communities in three cities here have already raised more money than the deployment's fuel will cost, and have no lawful way to get any of it there.

replies.text: Sail tonight and say so. Two partners asked and we answered in an hour — that is the story, and I want it told while it is true.

commitment.remembered: The government sailed the hospital ship within the hour of being asked and announced it loudly, with the six-week limit stated up front.

rejoinder.text: Four days, and the pictures are as good as pictures get. The host government accepted publicly and is now being asked at home why it took our ship, which is a question we made harder by answering in an hour with a camera.

replies.text: Sail tonight and say nothing. Let their government announce it as their decision, on their own morning. We still have the ship.

commitment.remembered: The government sailed the hospital ship without announcing it, and let the host government present the deployment as its own decision.

rejoinder.text: Their president announced it at nine on Friday as a request his government had made and won. Ours got a paragraph on page eleven at home, and one commentator asked why the administration had done nothing while somebody else's ship sailed.

replies.text: Sail, and stand up a lawful channel for the money three of our own cities have already raised. It is their families.

commitment.remembered: The government sailed the ship and opened a lawful channel for money raised at home to reach families in the affected country directly.

rejoinder.text: The channel moved more in eleven days than the deployment's fuel cost, and it took four agencies and a legal opinion nobody wanted to write. Two of the three cities have asked when we are doing it again.
